name: Pakistan Politics News
tagline: Islamabad, the provinces and Pakistan's place in the world.

articles.title: ECP Suspends All Preparations for Local Government Elections in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
articles.description: The Election Commission of Pakistan has suspended all steps for holding local government elections in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa until further orders, after a federal government order dated November 4 suspended Article 140-A of the Constitution across the province.
articles.sources: The Nation, November 5, 2026; Business Recorder, November 5, 2026; APP via Tez Khabar, November 5, 2026
articles.body:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has suspended all preparations for local government elections in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa until further orders, following a federal government order issued on November 4, 2026, reports said on Thursday, November 5.

The commission took the decision at a meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, which examined the federal government's Order No. 3, dated November 4. Under Clause 2 of the order, Article 140-A of the Constitution — which provides for the establishment of local governments in the provinces and assigns responsibility for conducting local government elections to the ECP — has been suspended, and the suspension has been extended to the remaining districts of the province.

What the suspension covers

According to the ECP, all steps taken so far to organise local government elections across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have been suspended, with no district exempt. The commission had earlier decided to hold the elections except in districts where Article 140-A had already been suspended following the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency in the province. The latest order removes that distinction, and the commission said it could not conduct the elections in the remaining districts while the constitutional provision stands suspended.

What happens next

The ECP has not shared a new polling date or given any timeframe for restarting the suspended process. The suspension is described as lasting until further notice, so the timing of any local government vote in the province now depends on whether the federal order is withdrawn or modified, or on a court ruling on the underlying emergency measures. Until then, the process of restoring elected local government institutions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa remains on hold.

articles.title: Opposition Agrees to Hold All Parties Conference Within 10 Days After Fazl Meeting
articles.description: Pakistan's opposition parties have agreed to hold an all parties conference within the next 10 days, decided at a meeting on November 4 at JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman's Islamabad residence, with committees formed to plan the gathering.
articles.sources: Dawn, November 5, 2026; The Express Tribune, November 5, 2026; Pakistan Today, November 5, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan's opposition parties have agreed to hold an all parties conference within the next 10 days, deciding the move at a meeting on Wednesday, November 4, at the Islamabad home of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, reports said on November 5.

Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai led the Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz-i-Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) delegation, with Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas beside him. Announcing the plan afterwards, Abbas said the conference would be held within a week to 10 days, and that committees had been formed to settle differences among the opposition parties and to plan the conference. Its date and agenda are to be announced by the committee.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa at the centre

The talks centred on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where governor's rule and an emergency were imposed on October 11, taking executive power from the PTI-led provincial government and handing it to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. It was the opposition's first joint meeting since those measures were imposed, and the conference is expected to take up the province's constitutional situation alongside the opposition's wider coordination.

Imran Khan's health raised

PTI leaders also used the occasion to raise the health of their founder, Imran Khan. Salman Akram Raja said Khan's blood pressure was not under control, and the party said it had surged to 192 a day before his meeting with his lawyer, Barrister Salman Safdar. Those figures come from the PTI's own account and have not been independently verified in the reports checked. The Islamabad High Court has fixed November 10 for hearing the appeals of Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi in the £190 million case, a date the opposition is also watching closely as the conference takes shape.

articles.title: Pakistan Tests Indigenous Fa'az Air-to-Air Missile, Its First Locally Developed Weapon of Its Kind
articles.description: Pakistan has successfully tested its Fa'az air-to-air missile, its first locally developed weapon of its kind, with the flight test conducted on November 3, the armed forces said — without disclosing range, speed or payload details.
articles.sources: PTI via Economic Times, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan has successfully tested its Fa'az air-to-air missile, its first locally developed air-to-air missile, in a push to strengthen its indigenous missile capabilities, PTI reported on November 4, citing an armed forces statement.

What was announced

The flight test was conducted on November 3. The missile is equipped with an advanced terminal guidance system and is designed to engage hostile aircraft at longer ranges, the statement said. The armed forces said the new weapon system would significantly expand the operational flexibility of the Pakistan Air Force. The statement did not disclose the missile's operational range, speed, payload specifications or other technical details, and those figures have not been stated here.

Reactions and recent tests

President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Army Chief Asim Munir congratulated the scientists and engineers, recognising their contribution to the indigenous weapon system, reports said. The Fa'az test comes amid a series of missile development and testing initiatives in recent months, including the January 2026 test of the indigenously developed Taimoor air-launched cruise missile, which has a reported range of 600 km and is designed to engage land and sea targets.

articles.title: UN Committee Reviews Pakistan's Progress on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights Today
articles.description: A UN committee reviews Pakistan's implementation of the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights in Geneva on Wednesday, with an 11-member delegation led by Minister of State for Law and Justice Aqeel Malik.
articles.sources: Dawn, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
A United Nations committee will review Pakistan's efforts to implement the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) during its eighth session in Geneva on Wednesday, Dawn reported on November 4.

Who is involved

The Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights is a body of 18 independent experts that monitors implementation of the ICESCR by its state parties. Barrister Aqeel Malik, the Minister of State for Law and Justice, will lead Pakistan's 11-member delegation to the session, which reviews the country's second periodic report under the covenant. The delegation includes Tahir Andrabi, Pakistan's Ambassador and Permanent Representative, the secretary to the Ministry of Human Rights, and Nayyab Ali, a consultant on transgender rights.

Why this session matters

The session takes place at a significant moment — the 60th anniversaries of the ICESCR and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights. The committee seeks a constructive dialogue with state parties, to determine whether the covenant's norms are being applied and how implementation and enforcement could be improved so people can enjoy these rights in full. Amnesty International is due to submit a briefing paper to coincide with Pakistan's second periodic review, Dawn reported. The committee's conclusions had not been published at the time of writing.

articles.title: Government Offers PTI Five Seats on Electoral Reforms Committee — and PTI Asks for the 2013 Formula
articles.description: The government has invited PTI to join a parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, with 15 government seats and five opposition seats proposed — but PTI's chief whip has asked for the consensus formula used in 2013 instead.
articles.sources: The Pakistan Daily, Pakistan Desk, ARY News, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
The government has invited Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to join a parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, with Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry telephoning PTI chief whip Amir Dogar, reports on November 3 said.

The proposed split

Under the proposed formula, 15 members of the government and five members of the opposition from the National Assembly would sit on the committee. Chaudhry asked Dogar to send PTI's names to the Speaker of the National Assembly as soon as possible so the notification forming the committee can be issued, Pakistan Desk reported.

Why PTI has not accepted yet

Dogar questioned what role the opposition could play with what he called extremely low representation, and asked for the formula used by the electoral reforms committee constituted in 2013, which operated by consensus across parties and produced the Elections Act 2017. He also demanded the committee first focus on investigating alleged electoral rigging. What has not been published is whether the committee has terms of reference, a timeline, or any remit over the Election Commission itself — so the test will be whether the government moves on the ratio or treats the offer as already made.

articles.title: ECP Issues Show-Cause Notice to MQM-P Over Missed Intra-Party Poll Deadline
articles.description: The Election Commission of Pakistan has issued a show-cause notice to MQM-P for failing to hold mandatory intra-party elections within the extended deadline of October 15, 2026, giving the party 14 days to explain.
articles.sources: Aaj English TV, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has issued a show-cause notice to the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) for failing to hold mandatory intra-party elections within the extended deadline of October 15, 2026, Aaj English TV reported on November 3.

What the notice says

According to the ECP, the notice was issued on October 26, giving the party 14 days to explain its failure to meet the legal requirement. Under the Elections Act 2017, political parties are required to hold regular elections for their office-bearers and submit an election certificate within seven days of completing the process.

What happens next

MQM-P must now respond within the 14-day window or face further action under the law, though the reports checked did not specify what sanction the Commission would seek if the party does not comply. The notice is a procedural step about internal party elections, not a finding about the party's electoral standing, and the party's response has not yet been reported.

articles.title: MQM-P Launches Street Movement for New Administrative Units, Announces November 29 Rally
articles.description: MQM-P chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui announced a 'historic rally' on Karachi's Sharea Faisal on November 29 and called for referendums on creating new administrative units, Dawn reported on November 2.
articles.sources: Dawn, The Nation, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) has launched a major mobilisation campaign for the creation of new administrative units, with party chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui announcing on Sunday a 'historic rally' on Sharea Faisal on November 29, Dawn reported on November 2.

What the party is demanding

Addressing a workers' convention at KMC Park in PIB Colony, Karachi, Dr Siddiqui — who is also the federal education minister — said the time had come for the oppressed to unite against 'an entrenched system of feudal domination and family-based politics.' He called for referendums under the Constitution to determine the will of the people on new administrative units in Sindh and the three other provinces, arguing the existing provincial structure had failed to deliver inclusive governance and equitable distribution of resources. Senior leader Dr Farooq Sattar echoed the referendum call at a District East workers' meeting.

A wider debate over provinces

The campaign lands amid a renewed national debate over restructuring the provincial system, following proposals by senior government figures for new provinces. Retired civil servants, diplomats and generals in the Roedad Khan Club warned in a statement shared with Dawn on Saturday against constitutional changes imposed without public consent, and rejected what they called hybrid governance. MQM-P leaders predicted the November 29 procession would fill roads leading to Sharea Faisal; whether the referendum demand gains traction with other parties remains to be seen.

articles.title: Pakistan Welcomes US Mediation Offer on Taliban Talks — With Conditions
articles.description: Pakistan's Foreign Office says it would welcome US efforts to facilitate talks with Afghanistan, provided Kabul takes verifiable action against militant groups — but no talks have been scheduled, reports said on November 2.
articles.sources: KhabarWire, Pakistan Today, The Express Tribune, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan's Foreign Office said on Sunday, November 1, that it would welcome US efforts to facilitate talks with Afghanistan, attaching a condition that Kabul take verifiable action against militant groups before meaningful negotiations can begin, Pakistan Today reported via KhabarWire on November 2.

The condition

'Pakistan would welcome sincere efforts by friendly countries, including the United States, to facilitate dialogue with Afghanistan,' Foreign Office spokesman Sajjad Haider Khan told Independent Urdu. He said any meaningful dialogue must rest on a 'clear commitment' by the Afghan Taliban authorities to take concrete, sustained and verifiable action against the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan, the Balochistan Liberation Army and other groups. The response followed remarks by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on Saturday, October 31, that Washington had 'obviously heard' Pakistan's concerns about attacks 'sponsored from the territory of Afghanistan' and that 'if there's a productive role for us to play, we'll play it.'

What is still uncertain

No date, venue or format for talks has been agreed, and Washington has not said whether it will formally take on the role of facilitator, KhabarWire noted, adding that no full official transcript of the Foreign Office remarks has been published. The exchange follows the Taliban saying its final efforts at dialogue had failed and Pakistan's information ministry calling cross-border terrorism a red line. Pakistan's statement is a response to a US remark, not a joint announcement — and Rubio's offer was itself conditional.

articles.title: PTI Hits Back at Shehbaz Sharif Over KP Criticism, Demands End to Governor's Rule
articles.description: PTI accused Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif of having no moral authority to lecture on democracy after he criticised the party's 13-year rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and demanded the release of Imran Khan and an end to governor's rule.
articles.sources: Business Recorder, November 1, 2026
articles.body:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf on Saturday launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif after he criticised the party's 13-year governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa at a PML-N parliamentary party meeting, Business Recorder reported on November 1.

What the PTI said

The party said the prime minister had no moral authority to lecture others on democracy, governance or public service, describing his premiership, in its words, as the product of a stolen mandate and backdoor deals, and accusing him of electoral manipulation and political engineering. It also said the Sohail Afridi-led provincial government had allocated substantial funds for police vehicles and operational requirements, but that federal institutions had failed to provide essential modern equipment. These are the PTI's claims, reported as its response, not findings by an independent body.

The demands that followed

The PTI condemned the continued detention of its founder Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, and demanded their release alongside all political prisoners, alleging that restrictions on political meetings and access to lawyers reflected fear of the party's popularity. It called for the withdrawal of governor's rule and emergency measures, restoration of the elected Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government, release of outstanding provincial funds and the province's rightful National Finance Commission share, reversal of controversial constitutional amendments, and fresh, free and fair general elections.

articles.title: China's CPC Minister Liu Haixing Arrives in Islamabad on First Official Visit
articles.description: Liu Haixing, minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China, arrived in Islamabad on Sunday on his first official visit to Pakistan, at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar.
articles.sources: Arab News, 24NewsHD, DNA News Agency, Foreign Office statement, November 1, 2026
articles.body:
Liu Haixing, minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, arrived in Islamabad on Sunday, November 1, on his first official visit to Pakistan, at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, the Foreign Office said, as reported by Arab News, 24NewsHD and DNA News Agency.

A meeting and a high-level event

During his visit, Liu will call on Pakistan's leadership and co-chair a high-level event with Dar on Monday, November 2, according to the Foreign Office statement. The International Department manages the CPC's relations with foreign political parties and organisations, and Liu assumed the post on September 30, 2025, 24NewsHD reported.

Party-to-party ties

The visit forms part of ongoing high-level and party-to-party exchanges between Pakistan and China, reflecting what the Foreign Office described as the two countries' shared commitment to further strengthening their All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership. The statement framed the trip as adding momentum to bilateral ties and deepening mutual understanding on regional and international issues of common interest; no new agreements were announced in the reports of his arrival.

articles.title: PPP Courts Opposition to Join 30-Member Electoral Reforms Committee
articles.description: A PPP delegation met opposition leaders on Friday to invite them into the proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, after the National Assembly approved the 30-member body.
articles.sources: Express Tribune, Dawn, The Nation, October 31, 2026
articles.body:
The Pakistan Peoples Party intensified its efforts on Friday to secure opposition participation in the proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, as a party delegation met Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas to urge him to join the initiative, The Express Tribune reported on October 31.

A 30-member committee, awaiting notification

The National Assembly has approved the formation of a 30-member parliamentary committee to oversee electoral reforms, comprising 20 members from the lower house and 10 from the Senate, with seats allocated to parliamentary parties in proportion to their numerical strength. Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the Speaker would soon issue a formal notification constituting the committee, while the process of finalising members' names was still under way. He added that the PTI had not opposed the motion when it was presented in the National Assembly.

Opposition seeks time to consult

The PPP delegation comprised Secretary General Nayyar Bokhari, Senator Waqar Mehdi, Nadeem Afzal Chan and Senator Sherry Rehman. Senator Rehman said Abbas had sought time to consult before conveying his response, adding that the party was hopeful of a positive outcome. Dawn reported that the PPP also urged opposition lawmakers to end their boycott and rejoin parliamentary standing committees, which they had quit in August 2025, and to engage with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif over the appointment of a new chief election commissioner. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan has demanded equal representation for government and opposition on the committee, and the opposition is expected to give a formal response after internal consultations.

articles.title: National Assembly Unanimously Passes Workplace Harassment Resolution as Parliament Is Prorogued
articles.description: The National Assembly unanimously passed a resolution against all forms of workplace harassment on Friday, before both houses of Parliament were prorogued, closing the current session.
articles.sources: The Nation, PakEra, October 31, 2026
articles.body:
The National Assembly on Friday unanimously passed a resolution reaffirming Parliament's commitment to protecting the dignity, equality and rights of every individual against all forms of workplace harassment and gender-based discrimination, The Nation reported on October 31.

What the resolution says

The resolution was moved by Dr Shahida Rehmani, Member of the National Assembly and Secretary of the Women's Parliamentary Caucus. It reaffirms the legislative intent and protections in the Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010, as amended in 2022, which expressly recognises discrimination on the basis of gender, whether sexual or non-sexual, within the statutory framework of harassment.

Both houses close their sessions

Both houses of Parliament were prorogued on Friday, October 30, ending the current session; neither house meets again until a new session is called. Before closing, the Senate passed two education bills already passed by the National Assembly — the Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (Amendment) Bill 2026 and the Pakistan Study Centres (Amendment) Bill 2026. A bill becomes an Act only after the President gives assent, so the education bills now await that step.

articles.title: National Assembly Passes Four Government Amendment Bills by Majority Vote
articles.description: The National Assembly passed four government amendment bills on October 30, 2026, after clause-by-clause consideration, covering higher education, engineering, textiles and the Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Authority.
articles.sources: Associated Press of Pakistan via UrduPoint, October 30, 2026.
articles.body:
The National Assembly on Friday passed four government bills by majority vote after clause-by-clause consideration, according to the Associated Press of Pakistan. The bills covered higher education, engineering education, textiles and the Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Authority.

The four bills

The bills passed were the Higher Education Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2026; the NFC Institute of Engineering and Technology Multan (Amendment) Bill, 2026; the National Textile University (Amendment) Bill, 2026; and the National Rahmatul-Lil-Aalameen Wa Khatamun Nabiyyin Authority (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

How they were passed

Each bill went through clause-by-clause consideration before being put to a vote, and all four were carried by majority vote. The passage adds to the House's legislative record for the current session, which has seen a mix of government business and procedural interruptions in recent days.

What happens next

Amendment bills of this kind typically move on to the Senate for consideration before they can become law. The education-related measures touch institutions that shape Pakistan's higher education and technical training landscape, while the textiles university bill concerns a sector that remains central to the country's export economy.

Further details of the amendments, including their specific provisions, will become clearer as the bills proceed through the remaining stages of the legislative process.

articles.title: Opposition Signals Willingness to Join Electoral Reforms Committee After PPP Outreach
articles.description: Opposition leaders have indicated they are willing to join a proposed 30-member parliamentary committee on electoral reforms after outreach by the Pakistan Peoples Party, Geo News reported on October 30, 2026.
articles.sources: Geo News and 24NewsHD, October 30, 2026.
articles.body:
Opposition leaders have indicated their willingness to join a proposed parliamentary committee on electoral reforms following an outreach by the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), with a formal response expected after consultations within the next few days, according to Geo News.

The PPP outreach

A PPP delegation met opposition leaders at the Parliament House in Islamabad on October 30, on the instructions of party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, and invited them to become part of the electoral reforms committee. The PPP delegation included former Senate chairman Nayyer Bokhari, Senator Sherry Rehman, Senator Waqar Mehdi and Nadeem Afzal Chan. Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayin-e-Pakistan chief and National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas attended, along with PTI leaders Senator Ali Zafar, Senator Noorul Haq Qadri and Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai.

A 30-member panel

Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the National Assembly had already approved the formation of the electoral reforms committee and that the Speaker would soon issue its formal notification, with the finalisation of members' names still under way. The proposed committee would comprise 30 parliamentarians — 20 from the National Assembly and 10 from the Senate — with seats distributed among political parties according to their numerical strength in the two houses. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan has demanded equal representation for the government and opposition on the panel.

What the committee would examine

According to reports, the committee is expected to examine alleged rigging in the 2024 general elections as well as subsequent by-elections and elections in Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, with its recommendations to be presented before parliament for approval. The PPP proposed that the government and opposition jointly formulate recommendations aimed at ensuring transparent, free and fair elections.

Achakzai and Abbas sought time to consult the PTI leadership before giving a formal response, so the opposition's participation is signalled rather than confirmed for now.

articles.title: National Assembly Session Suspended After Speaker Finds House Lacks Quorum
articles.description: Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq suspended the National Assembly on October 29, 2026, after a headcount confirmed the House lacked quorum, delaying its planned legislative business.
articles.sources: Public news reports, October 2026.
articles.body:
The National Assembly session was suspended on Thursday after the Speaker found that the House did not have the required number of members present. Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq ordered a break in proceedings once a headcount confirmed that quorum was incomplete, according to reports of the session.

How the session unfolded

The session began at 11:09 a.m. under the chairmanship of Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq. Soon after proceedings commenced, Mian Fayyaz Hussain Chhajrra pointed out the absence of quorum, prompting the Speaker to order a headcount. After the count, the Speaker declared that the House was not in order and announced a break until the quorum was completed.

Business left on the agenda

The House had been expected to take up calling attention notices, motions, the introduction of bills, resolutions and other legislative business. Those items were delayed by the suspension, a recurring procedural hurdle when attendance falls short of the required threshold.

Why quorum matters

Quorum rules exist to ensure that decisions of the House are taken with a minimum level of participation from elected members. When the threshold is not met, proceedings cannot continue, and the sitting is paused until enough members return to the chamber.

The suspension is a procedural pause rather than an adjournment of the session itself, and the House is expected to resume once quorum is restored.

articles.title: Pakistan Proposes Parliamentary Friendship Group With Turkmenistan
articles.description: Pakistan has proposed a parliamentary friendship group in Turkmenistan's parliament to deepen dialogue and cooperation, discussed in Islamabad on October 29, 2026.
articles.sources: Public news reports, October 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan has proposed establishing a parliamentary friendship group in Turkmenistan's parliament to strengthen inter-parliamentary dialogue and expand bilateral cooperation, according to a press release from Pakistan's National Assembly reported on October 29.

The Islamabad meeting

The proposal was discussed at a meeting between Pakistan's Parliamentary Friendship Group with Turkmenistan, led by its convener Sanjay Perwani, and Turkmenistan's Ambassador to Pakistan, Atadjan Movlamov, at the Parliament House in Islamabad. Members of Pakistan's National Assembly, including Fateh Ullah Khan and Khawaja Izhar ul Hassan, also attended.

A long-standing relationship

Perwani highlighted the longstanding relations between the two countries, recalling Pakistan's early recognition of Turkmenistan's independence and reaffirming support for the country's policy of permanent neutrality. Pakistan and Turkmenistan established diplomatic relations on May 10, 1992.

What cooperation covers

The participants discussed ways to strengthen parliamentary relations and expand cooperation between the two countries, including continued high-level engagement, parliamentary exchanges and cooperation on regional and international issues. Energy and regional connectivity remain key areas of bilateral cooperation, particularly the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India (TAPI) gas pipeline project, alongside discussions on electricity transmission and fibre-optic connectivity.

The meeting concluded with a reaffirmation of the commitment to strengthening bilateral relations through parliamentary diplomacy, trade and economic cooperation, and closer people-to-people ties.

articles.title: Lahore High Court Judge Mohsin Akhtar Kayani Resigns, Citing Executive Grip on Judiciary
articles.description: Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani resigned from the Lahore High Court, saying the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments compromised the independence of the high courts.
articles.sources: Gulf News, Dawn and Geo News reports, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
A senior Pakistani judge resigned on Wednesday, accusing the executive of increasing its control over the judiciary and warning that recent constitutional amendments had undermined the independence of the country's high courts. Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani of the Lahore High Court said his conscience no longer permitted him to remain on the bench, describing the decision as painful after more than a decade of judicial service.

What the resignation letter says

In a letter addressed to Pakistan's president, reported by Dawn and Geo News, Kayani cited personal reasons, including health concerns following recent surgery, alongside serious concerns about the direction of the judicial system. "In my considered view, the changes introduced through the Twenty-sixth and Twenty-seventh Constitutional Amendments have compromised the independence and institutional integrity of the High Courts," he wrote. "I have witnessed what I regard as the executive's growing control over judicial institutions, extending to the appointment and transfer of judges."

Kayani said he was particularly troubled by the plight of ordinary people seeking justice, arguing that their needs had increasingly been neglected, and that such interference had seriously eroded public confidence in judicial independence and the fairness of legal proceedings. His resignation lands in a charged moment for Pakistan's judiciary, where debate over the amendments and the balance between parliament and the courts has become one of the defining arguments of the year.

articles.title: Pakistan Says Afghan Firing Kills One in South Waziristan Border District
articles.description: One person was killed and five injured after Afghan Taliban fired at civilian houses and a market in Pakistan's Waziristan region, a senior Pakistani official said.
articles.sources: Reuters, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
One person was killed and five injured after Afghan Taliban fired at civilian houses and a market in Pakistan's Waziristan region near the countries' border, a senior Pakistani administrative official said on Wednesday. Pakistani forces are "responding effectively and heavily" to the "unprovoked" firing on Tuesday, the Deputy Commissioner of South Waziristan Lower said.

Afghan Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment on the incident. The violence comes days after the Afghan Taliban said that problems with Pakistan can be resolved through diplomacy, a statement that now sits uneasily beside fresh casualties on the frontier.

Pakistan and Afghanistan have increasingly been at odds over militancy, with Islamabad accusing Kabul of harbouring militants who stage cross-border attacks. The Taliban government denies the charge and says militancy is Pakistan's internal problem. The conflict between the neighbours has killed hundreds of people this year, and each new border incident makes the diplomatic track harder to sustain.

articles.title: Pakistan Marks Kashmir Black Day With Rallies Across the Country
articles.description: Rallies were held across Pakistan on October 27 to mark Kashmir Black Day, with the prime minister, the National Assembly deputy speaker and provincial leaders reaffirming support for the Kashmiri people's right to self-determination.
articles.sources: UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News (APP), October 27, 2026; The Europe Today, October 27, 2026.
articles.body:
Rallies and demonstrations were held across Pakistan on Tuesday, October 27, to mark Kashmir Black Day, with participants condemning India's control of Jammu and Kashmir and calling for a peaceful settlement of the dispute through United Nations resolutions. Protests were reported from Peshawar to Muzaffarabad, and from Gwadar to Chitral, according to Associated Press of Pakistan reports.

In Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi led the main protest rally, which was attended by the governor's advisers, Hurriyat leader Daud Khan Yousafzai, government officials, employees and a large number of students. Participants observed one minute of silence to express solidarity with the Kashmiri people.

What leaders said

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, in a message marking the day, said Pakistan's position on Jammu and Kashmir remained clear, consistent and principled, and that lasting peace and stability in South Asia could not be achieved without a just and peaceful resolution of the dispute in line with the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people. He said Pakistan would continue to extend moral, diplomatic and political support to the Kashmiri people at every national and international forum.

The prime minister recalled that the landing of Indian forces in Srinagar on October 27, 1947, marked the beginning of what he described as a tragic chapter in the history of Jammu and Kashmir, and said the Kashmiri people had since been denied the realisation of their right to self-determination as affirmed in UN resolutions.

In the National Assembly, Deputy Speaker Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah said October 27 was observed to condemn India's occupation of Jammu and Kashmir and to express solidarity with Kashmiris seeking the right to self-determination. He said the people and the National Assembly of Pakistan stood with their Kashmiri brethren, and paid tribute to the resilience of the Kashmiri people.

Why October 27 is observed

Pakistan observes October 27 every year as Kashmir Black Day to protest the arrival of Indian troops in Srinagar in 1947. The day is marked by rallies, seminars and official statements, with the government and political parties repeating the call for a settlement based on UN resolutions. Organisers of Tuesday's rallies said the demonstrations were intended to draw the international community's attention to the dispute and to the Kashmiri people's demand for self-determination.

articles.title: National Assembly Passes Seven Private Members' Bills, Sends Six to Committees
articles.description: The National Assembly on October 27 passed seven private members' bills after clause-by-clause consideration and referred six more bills to standing committees for further deliberation.
articles.sources: UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News (APP), October 27, 2026.
articles.body:
The National Assembly on Tuesday passed seven private members' bills by majority vote after clause-by-clause consideration, Associated Press of Pakistan reported. The bills cleared by the House covered science and technology, corporate social responsibility, evidence law, senior citizens, criminal procedure and children's rights.

The bills passed included the Pakistan Council for Science and Technology (Amendment) Bill, 2025; the Corporate Social Responsibility Bill, 2026; the Qanun-e-Shahadat (Amendment) Bill, 2026; the Islamabad Capital Territory Senior Citizens (Amendment) Bill, 2025; the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Bill, 2024 (Schedule-II); the National Commission on the Rights of Child (Amendment) Bill, 2025; and the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2025.

Six bills sent to committees

Meanwhile, six other bills were referred to the relevant committees for further deliberation and review. These included the Factories (Amendment) Bill, 2025, to amend the Factories Act, 1934; the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) (Amendment) Bill, 2024, to amend the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act, 2021; and the Islamabad Rent Restriction (Amendment) Bill, 2025, to amend the Islamabad Rent Restriction Ordinance, 2001.

Also referred to committees were the National Highways Safety (Amendment) Bill, 2025, to amend the National Highways Safety Ordinance, 2000; the Payment of Wages (Amendment) Bill, 2025, to amend the Payment of Wages Act, 1936; and the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2025, seeking amendments to the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

Parliamentary business continues

Private members' bills are legislation introduced by members who are not ministers, and their passage through clause-by-clause consideration is part of the Assembly's regular legislative work. Bills referred to committees will return to the House after the committees complete their deliberations, at which point members can debate and vote on them. The Assembly's handling of a large batch of bills in a single sitting reflects the volume of pending legislative business before the House.

articles.title: Pakistan Strongly Condemns Houthi Missile Attacks Near Makkah and Madinah
articles.description: Pakistan's Foreign Office on October 26 condemned ballistic missile attacks reported on October 24 targeting Saudi Arabia's Makkah and Madinah regions, calling them a grave violation of Saudi sovereignty.
articles.sources: The Express Tribune, October 26, 2026; Dunya News, October 26, 2026; Dawn, October 26, 2026.
articles.body:
Pakistan on Monday strongly condemned ballistic missile attacks reported on October 24 that targeted Saudi Arabia's Makkah and Madinah regions, including areas near Islam's holiest sites. The Foreign Office said the attacks were reprehensible and constituted a grave violation of Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

What the Foreign Office said

Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said the attacks demonstrated a blatant disregard for the sanctity of Islam's holiest sites and for the safety of civilians. In a statement shared by the ministry, Pakistan reiterated what it described as its unwavering solidarity with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its firm commitment to the Makkah Alliance. The statement also reaffirmed Pakistan's support for the security, stability and defence of Saudi Arabia, including the protection of the Two Holy Mosques, against any external aggression or threat.

Interceptions reported on October 24

Reports on October 24 said Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence briefly issued alerts warning of potential danger in Taif and Yanbu, as well as in Makkah and Jeddah, before later saying the threat had passed. A Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired towards Taif and Yanbu. Dawn reported that debris from intercepted missiles fell in the Makkah and Madinah regions, including Wadi al-Mughammas in Makkah and areas of Jeddah, Taif and Rabigh. The Houthis subsequently denied targeting Makkah and Madinah, saying their operations were directed at Saudi oil facilities and military bases, according to Dawn.

Why the condemnation matters

The condemnation comes at a moment of heightened regional tension, with fighting between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis having shattered a United Nations-brokered truce reached in 2022 that had largely halted cross-border attacks. Pakistan also commended what it called the vigilance and efficiency of Saudi air defence forces in countering the attacks. Earlier in October, the Foreign Office had separately condemned an attack on a power distribution station in Madinah on September 29, describing an attack on civilian infrastructure supplying electricity to the Prophet's Mosque as a grave provocation. Monday's statement fits a consistent pattern: Islamabad publicly aligning itself with Riyadh's security whenever holy sites or Saudi territory are reported to be under threat, while stopping short of announcing any new military step of its own.

What happens next

For now, the statement is diplomatic rather than operational. It signals solidarity and reaffirms existing defence commitments, but it does not announce fresh deployments or new agreements. Attention now turns to whether regional diplomacy, including reported talks involving Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, can lower tensions before further attacks are reported. Readers should treat claims about the targets and the scale of any attack as reported by the respective sides, since the two sides have given different accounts of what was struck.

articles.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye Reported to Hold Tehran Talks on De-escalation
articles.description: Senior officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were reported to be meeting Iranian officials in Tehran on October 26 to discuss regional security and efforts to prevent a wider escalation.
articles.sources: CNN-News18, October 26, 2026; Abb Takk News, October 26, 2026.
articles.body:
Senior officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were reported to be meeting Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday, October 26, to discuss regional security and efforts to prevent a wider escalation in the Middle East. The talks were described in reports as a de-escalation push at a time of rising tensions across the region, including reported missile and drone attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis against Saudi Arabia.

Who was reported to attend

Reports named Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin as part of the delegation heading to Tehran. Those names come from news reports rather than an official joint statement, and the precise agenda and format of the meeting had not been publicly confirmed by all sides at the time of reporting. Readers should therefore treat the attendance list as reported, not as an officially confirmed delegation.

The Makkah pact backdrop

The meeting comes against the backdrop of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye in August. Under that pact, the three countries committed to treating an armed attack against one member as an attack against all, raising important questions about collective security as regional hostilities intensify. The agreement has drawn close attention because it links three major regional players in a formal defence understanding, and any discussion in Tehran would inevitably be read in that light. Pakistan has also played an intermediary role in efforts to reduce tensions between Washington and Tehran, according to the reports, adding another layer to its involvement.

What is at stake

The stakes are high. Attacks near Saudi Arabia's holy cities, reported strikes on energy infrastructure and the risk of miscalculation all raise the danger of a wider conflict that could disrupt shipping, energy supplies and the safety of millions of people living and working in the Gulf. A meeting in Tehran, if it takes place as reported, would at minimum signal that direct channels between Riyadh, Islamabad, Ankara and Tehran remain open even during a crisis. Diplomats often use such channels to clarify intentions, warn against escalation and explore off-ramps that public statements alone cannot deliver.

What to watch for

The Tehran meeting will be watched for any sign of diplomatic progress, regional coordination or a pathway to prevent further escalation. No outcome had been announced in the reports available on October 26, and it would be wrong to present the talks as a breakthrough before any joint statement or official readout appears. What can be said is that the reported timing, on the same day Pakistan publicly condemned attacks near Makkah and Madinah, underlines how closely Islamabad's diplomacy and its public messaging are moving together in this crisis.

articles.title: Pakistan LPG Shortage Worsens as Iran Border Crossings Close
articles.description: The closure of the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings has halted LPG imports from Iran, pushing cylinder prices sharply higher and stranding hundreds of trucks.
articles.sources: Reuters, October 23, 2026; Pakistan LPG Association; Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry.
articles.body:
Pakistan is facing a worsening shortage of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) after the closure of two key border crossings with Iran halted imports, traders said, driving up prices for households that depend on gas cylinders for cooking and heating. The Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings were closed on October 17, cutting off a supply route that delivers a large share of Pakistan's daily LPG imports.

Why the closure matters so much

Pakistan imports about 7,000 metric tons of LPG a day from Iran, according to the Pakistan LPG Association. More than 4,000 tons a day enters through Gabd-Rimdan alone, said Shamsul Haq, former president of the Gwadar Chamber of Commerce and Industry. With both crossings shut, that flow stopped. "These imports are at halt," Haq said. The Balochistan government, in the province where the crossings are located, said the temporary closure was intended to address security concerns and curb smuggling, while Iran's foreign ministry cited technical issues. The two sides giving different reasons has left traders and transporters uncertain about when normal crossings will resume.

Prices jump and trucks pile up

Traders said the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder had risen to 7,000 rupees from 4,500 rupees within days, and warned it could climb further if the disruptions persist. For low-income households, that jump is a direct hit on the weekly budget, since a cylinder that lasted a household through its cooking needs suddenly costs more than half as much again. Hundreds of trucks, including LPG tankers, are stranded on both sides of the border, Haq said, and the Quetta Chamber of Commerce and Industry has advised members to stop placing new orders with Iran until further notice. Truck drivers stuck at the crossings said they had been waiting for days in harsh conditions with limited access to basic amenities. "We have been standing here for over a week waiting for the border to open," said Abdul Ghani Baloch, one affected driver.

A partial reopening, and a wider trade stake

There was some relief in the week: the Gabd-Rimdan crossing reopened for Pakistani exports of perishable goods, although more than 1,000 Pakistani containers carrying potatoes, bananas and rice for Iran were also reported stranded. Pakistan LPG Association chairman Irfan Khokhar warned shortages and price increases could worsen if imports do not resume soon. The episode also underlines how much ordinary trade rides on these crossings. Pakistan-Iran trade totalled about $2.8 billion in the 2023-24 fiscal year, including roughly $684 million of Pakistani exports, according to the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry. Until the crossings fully reopen, households, traders and transporters alike will be watching the border for the first sign of LPG tankers moving again.

articles.title: Pakistan Ends Machine-Readable Passports and Switches Fully to E-Passports
articles.description: From October 23, 2026, passport offices in Pakistan and missions abroad issue only e-passports. Valid machine-readable passports remain usable until expiry.
articles.sources: The Nation, October 24, 2026; Geo News; Directorate General of Immigration and Passports.
articles.body:
Pakistan has discontinued the issuance of traditional machine-readable passports (MRPs), with all passport offices across the country and Pakistani diplomatic missions abroad switching exclusively to e-passports from October 23, 2026. According to the Directorate General of Immigration and Passports, the move marks the end of the 22-year-old machine-readable passport system as the country completes its transition to electronic passports.

What changes for applicants

Anyone applying for a new passport, or renewing an expired one, will now receive an e-passport. The directorate said all passport offices in Pakistan and diplomatic missions abroad were now issuing only e-passports, completing the transition to the upgraded passport system. The change follows a statement by the interior ministry in the National Assembly, when it informed lawmakers that the issuance of machine-readable passports would be discontinued within a month. Responding to a question raised by MNA Malik Shakir Bashir Awan during the question-and-answer session, the ministry had said that passport offices and Pakistani missions abroad would subsequently issue only e-passports.

What stays the same for existing holders

Citizens holding valid machine-readable passports will be allowed to continue using them until their expiry dates, and do not need to replace a valid document simply because the system has changed. Once expired, these passports will not be eligible for renewal under the previous system, and holders will be required to obtain e-passports instead. That distinction matters for the many Pakistanis living abroad, who often plan travel around passport validity: a valid MRP remains a valid travel document until the date printed in it, but the next document in hand will be an electronic one.

A transition four years in the making

Pakistan introduced e-passports in March 2022, initially making the facility available to diplomats and residents of Islamabad. In August 2023, the facility was extended to all Pakistani citizens, who were given the option of obtaining either a machine-readable passport or an e-passport. Before the introduction of machine-readable passports, Pakistan issued handwritten passports, a practice dating back to the country's independence in 1947. The e-passport carries an electronic chip storing the holder's personal and biometric information, which authorities say strengthens travel-document security and makes identity verification more effective in line with international standards. For applicants, the practical advice is simple: check the expiry date on your current passport, and when renewal time comes, expect the new electronic format. Applicants should also budget for higher fees reported for the new document: Pakistan Observer reported the normal fee for a 36-page e-passport valid for five years at Rs9,000, against Rs4,500 for the machine-readable equivalent, with urgent and fast-track e-passport fees reported at Rs15,000 and Rs22,000 respectively.

articles.title: Pakistan Calls for a Fairer Global Order at the United Nations
articles.description: Acting permanent representative Ambassador Usman Jadoon pressed for Security Council reform, inclusive governance of military AI and human control over autonomous weapons.
articles.sources: Dawn, October 24, 2026; Radio Pakistan.
articles.body:
Pakistan has called for a more representative international order and consistent application of international law during a series of debates at the United Nations this week, with its interventions covering Security Council reform, military artificial intelligence (AI), weapons of mass destruction, radiation safety, human rights and conflicts in the Middle East. The message, delivered in New York, highlighted the need to balance international security with accountability and the interests of developing countries.

No new permanent seats, Pakistan argues

Addressing the General Assembly, Pakistan's acting permanent representative, Ambassador Usman Jadoon, opposed creating additional permanent seats on the Security Council, arguing that this would perpetuate existing inequalities. "The question is not whether the Council should be reformed, but how to make it more representative, democratic, transparent and accountable," he said. Pakistan favoured expanding elected, non-permanent membership through regular elections and fair regional rotation, while seeking adequate representation for Africa and other underrepresented regions. The position restates a long-standing Pakistani argument: that adding permanent members, with or without veto powers, would entrench historical privilege rather than democratise the Council, while a larger elected membership would tilt the balance toward the wider membership.

Military AI and human control

On military AI, Mr Jadoon called for inclusive, UN-led governance, warning that the technology could accelerate military decision-making and increase escalation risks, particularly in situations involving nuclear weapons. He also stressed the need for meaningful human control over autonomous weapons systems. At the General Assembly's First Committee, Counsellor Syed Atif Raza warned that advances in AI, synthetic biology and the life and chemical sciences were creating new security risks, and called for safeguards against the misuse of scientific developments without restricting developing countries' access to peaceful applications. Pakistan reaffirmed its commitments under the biological and chemical weapons conventions, stressing the importance of verification and international cooperation.

Why developing countries are central to the argument

Running through Pakistan's interventions was a single thread: rules written without the developing world will not hold. Whether the subject is who sits on the Security Council, who governs military AI, or who gets access to peaceful scientific applications, Islamabad argued that legitimacy comes from representation and consistent application of the law, not from power alone. For a country that is both a major troop contributor to UN peacekeeping and a host to one of the UN's oldest observer missions, the argument carries practical weight as well as principle. The debates continue in the General Assembly, but Pakistan's position for this session is now on the record: reform the Council by electing more members, govern new weapons technologies together, and keep human beings in control of decisions about war.
